metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code with a deployable entry point (@WebService JAX-WS endpoint) present alongside a WSDL contract and Oracle database connection. Single-service Java WAR deployed on JBoss AS 5.1.
metadata.archetype_justification: The service has a database connection with write operations (INSERT into partner_orders) and accepts partner purchase orders via SOAP. It owns persistent state and exposes a CRUD-like operation.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Overall score 1.18 yields Not Ready band (< 1.5) but 11 High findings match the 2-11 High rule for Remediation Required tier. This divergence occurs because the system scores universally low across all categories (extreme legacy state with nearly all questions at score 1) while the count-based classification caps at Remediation Required for 2-11 High findings.

decomposition_strategy.rationale: Single-endpoint SOAP service with simple logic. Build a new cloud-native REST service alongside, migrate partners incrementally, decommission legacy.

effort_factors.module_boundaries: No modules but very simple logic — low complexity to rewrite
effort_factors.data_coupling: Single table, simple schema — low effort
effort_factors.communication_patterns: Pure sync SOAP — medium effort for partner migration
effort_factors.cicd_maturity: None — must be built from scratch

findings.title: No Managed Compute — All Workloads on JBoss AS 5.1/RHEL 6
findings.description: All compute runs on JBoss AS 5.1 on RHEL 6. No managed container orchestration, no serverless, no auto-scaling.
findings.gap: No managed compute services in use. All infrastructure is self-managed on an EOL application server and OS.
findings.recommendation: Containerize the application and deploy to ECS/Fargate or EKS. Alternatively, rewrite as a Lambda function behind API Gateway given the service's simplicity.

findings.title: Self-Managed Oracle 11g Database — No Managed Service
findings.description: Database is Oracle 11g at jdbc:oracle:thin:@10.0.9.30:1521:PARTDB — self-managed on-premises with raw JDBC DriverManager.getConnection() per request.
findings.gap: Self-managed database on EOL engine with no managed service benefits (automated failover, patching, backups, scaling).
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS PostgreSQL or Aurora PostgreSQL using AWS DMS. The schema is simple making migration straightforward.

findings.title: No Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: No workflow orchestration service in use. The single operation is implemented inline with no error handling or retry logic.
findings.gap: No orchestration — all logic hardcoded in the endpoint method. No retry or compensation patterns.
findings.recommendation: If the service grows to handle multi-step order processing, adopt Step Functions for orchestration.

findings.title: No Async Messaging Infrastructure
findings.description: No messaging infrastructure. Entirely synchronous SOAP. Order creation events are not published for downstream systems.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes cross service boundaries. Order events are invisible to downstream consumers.
findings.recommendation: Introduce managed messaging (SQS/SNS or EventBridge) to publish order events for downstream consumers.

findings.title: No Network Security Controls
findings.description: No network security configuration found. Plain HTTP on internal hostname with no VPC, security groups, or segmentation evidence.
findings.gap: No in-repo network security controls. Service directly exposed on internal network.
findings.recommendation: Deploy in a VPC with private subnets. Place application behind ALB/API Gateway. Restrict database access via security groups.

findings.title: No API Gateway or Load Balancer
findings.description: Service exposed directly on JBoss port 8080 with no managed entry point. No throttling, validation, or centralized auth.
findings.gap: Direct service exposure with no managed entry point providing throttling, auth, or request validation.
findings.recommendation: Place an API Gateway or ALB in front of the service with request validation and throttling.

findings.title: No Auto-Scaling
findings.description: Single JBoss instance with static capacity. No ASG, no ECS scaling, no Lambda concurrency management.
findings.gap: All capacity statically provisioned. Cannot respond to traffic spikes or scale down.
findings.recommendation: After containerization, configure ECS service auto-scaling or EKS HPA.

findings.title: No Backup and Recovery Configuration
findings.description: No backup configuration found. Oracle database has no in-repo backup plan, retention period, or PITR configuration.
findings.gap: No backup or recovery automation. Data loss risk with no documented restore procedure.
findings.recommendation: After migrating to RDS/Aurora, enable automated backups with PITR. Create and test a restore runbook.

findings.title: Zero Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: 0% IaC coverage. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or any IaC files. All infrastructure manually provisioned.
findings.gap: No IaC — all infrastructure created manually (ClickOps). Cannot reproduce environments.
findings.recommendation: Adopt CDK or Terraform to define all infrastructure. Start with database (RDS) and compute (ECS/Lambda), then networking and monitoring.

findings.title: No CI/CD Automation — All Manual
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Build uses Ant with wsgen/wsimport run by hand. No automated build, test, or deploy stages.
findings.gap: All deployments manual — no quality gates, no automated testing, no reproducible releases.
findings.recommendation: Create CI/CD pipeline (CodePipeline + CodeBuild or GitHub Actions) with build, test, security scan, and deploy stages.

findings.title: Legacy Java 6 with Obsolete JAX-WS Framework
findings.description: Java 6 with JAX-WS (RPC/encoded SOAP). All three axes regressed: language (Java 6 EOL 2013), framework (JAX-WS obsolete), AWS SDK (absent).
findings.gap: Compound legacy — language version, framework, and SDK all severely regressed.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Java 17+ with Spring Boot 3.x and AWS SDK v2. Replace SOAP with REST or gRPC.

findings.title: Tightly-Coupled Single-Class Monolith
findings.description: Entire application is one Java class with XML parsing, database access, and business logic in a single method. No module boundaries, no separation of concerns.
findings.gap: No module boundaries — all logic in a single method of a single class.
findings.recommendation: Apply Strangler Fig pattern: build new cloud-native service alongside legacy, migrate partners incrementally.

findings.title: All Communication Synchronous — No Async Patterns
findings.description: All communication is synchronous SOAP. No async messaging, no event publishing, no queue consumption. For a stateful-crud service, this means order state changes cannot propagate without coupling.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous HTTP with no async patterns.
findings.recommendation: Introduce async event publishing (SNS/EventBridge) for order creation events while maintaining synchronous partner response.

findings.title: No Async Process Handling
findings.description: All operations synchronous. No timeout protection, no async fallback. While the current INSERT is likely fast, no pattern exists for handling potential long-running operations.
findings.gap: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. No timeout protection.
findings.recommendation: If service scope expands to long-running operations, implement async processing with SQS and status polling.

findings.title: No API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No versioning. Single WSDL namespace with no version indicator. Breaking changes deployed directly to all partners.
findings.gap: No versioning — breaking changes deployed directly with no backward compatibility.
findings.recommendation: When modernizing to REST, adopt URL-path versioning (/v1/orders) with backward compatibility guarantees.

findings.title: All Endpoints Hard-Coded — No Service Discovery
findings.description: Database URL and service endpoint are string literals in source code. No service discovery, no configuration externalization.
findings.gap: All service endpoints hard-coded in application code.
findings.recommendation: Externalize configuration via environment variables or SSM Parameter Store. Adopt Cloud Map for service discovery.

findings.title: No Managed Object Storage for Partner Documents
findings.description: Partner XML purchase orders parsed in-memory and stored as structured columns. Raw XML not preserved. No S3, no document parsing pipeline.
findings.gap: Data on local/database storage with no managed object storage. Raw XML discarded after parsing.
findings.recommendation: Store raw partner XML submissions in S3 for audit, reprocessing, and analytics. Add lifecycle policies for archival.

findings.title: No Data Access Layer — Raw JDBC Inline
findings.description: Raw JDBC with string-concatenated SQL directly in the endpoint method. No DAO, no repository layer, no ORM. SQL injection vulnerability.
findings.gap: Database queries inline with no abstraction. SQL injection due to string concatenation.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a data access layer with parameterized queries (PreparedStatement at minimum, or Spring Data JPA).

findings.title: Oracle 11g — Well Past End-of-Life
findings.description: Oracle 11g reached end of extended support in 2021. No version pinning in IaC (no IaC exists). EOL engine with unpatched vulnerabilities.
findings.gap: Database engine at EOL with no version management or upgrade procedure.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Aurora PostgreSQL 15+ or RDS PostgreSQL 16 using AWS SCT and DMS.

findings.title: No Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption configuration. Oracle connection shows no TDE. Partner order data stored unencrypted.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest for sensitive partner data.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to RDS/Aurora, enable encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS key.

findings.title: No API Authentication Implemented
findings.description: No authentication logic in source code. submitOrder method accepts any request without identity verification.
findings.gap: No API authentication in the implementation despite claims of WS-Security.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-request authentication. Use API Gateway with OAuth2/JWT authorizers when modernizing.

findings.title: No Centralized Identity Provider
findings.description: No centralized IdP integration. Partner credentials in a flat properties file. No Cognito, OIDC, or SAML.
findings.gap: Application manages own authentication with no external IdP integration.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Cognito or external IdP for partner authentication with JWT tokens.

findings.title: Hardcoded Database Credentials in Source Code
findings.description: Database credentials hardcoded as string literals: DB_USER='partner_app', DB_PASS='partner2009'. Committed to version control.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in source code — critical security vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Immediately rotate credentials. Move all secrets to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation. Scrub git history.

findings.title: No Compute Hardening or Patching Strategy
findings.description: No patching evidence. RHEL 6 (EOL 2020), JBoss AS 5.1 (unsupported), Java 6 (unpatched vulnerabilities). No vulnerability scanning.
findings.gap: All runtime components are EOL with unpatched vulnerabilities and no scanning.
findings.recommendation: After containerization, use hardened base images (Amazon Linux 2023). Enable ECR scanning and Inspector.

findings.title: No Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD exists, so no security scanning. No SAST, DAST, or dependency scanning. Known vulnerabilities (SQL injection, XXE) persist.
findings.gap: No security scanning tools. Known vulnerabilities persist undetected.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST (SonarQube/Semgrep), dependency scanning (Dependabot), and container scanning into CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: No Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No tracing instrumented. No X-Ray, OpenTelemetry, or trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: Cannot trace requests or diagnose production issues.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with AWS X-Ray or OpenTelemetry after modernization.

findings.title: No SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no latency monitoring, no error rate tracking.
findings.gap: No SLOs — cannot measure whether system meets partner expectations.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for order submission (p99 latency, error rate). Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: No Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No tracking of order volume, partner activity, or error patterns.
findings.gap: No business metrics — cannot measure business outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Publish CloudWatch metrics for orders per partner, error rate by type, processing latency.

findings.title: No Anomaly Detection or Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection. Failures are silent.
findings.gap: No alerting — failures invisible until partners complain.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms on error rate and latency. Enable anomaly detection for order volume.

findings.title: Zero Automated Tests
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. README states 'No tests; partner onboarding is a manual SOAP-UI session.'
findings.gap: No integration tests, no unit tests. Regression risk completely unmanaged.
findings.recommendation: Create integration tests for order submission. Add test containers for DB testing. Include in CI pipeline.

findings.title: No Observability Ownership
findings.description: No dashboards, no named alarm owners, no CODEOWNERS. No monitoring infrastructure exists to own.
findings.gap: No observability ownership — monitoring is non-existent.
findings.recommendation: After establishing monitoring, define ownership via CODEOWNERS or team tags.
